svg.title: Contact CRM tracker: messages in, structured memory out
svg.desc: A message from an allowlisted contact passes the DM access gate into that contact's session and one agent turn: guard chain, behavior files, extraction, then memory_apply into canonical memory, and a short reply on the same channel. Questions from the web UI reach the same kind of turn and read memory with memory_search; an optional daily job summarizes the day.

g.text: Hover a box for what happens there; its connections light up. Click it to open the recipe section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: Contact CRM tracker: messages in, structured memory out
Event-driven: no cron job is required. The numbered steps are the recipe's Workflow list; the same turn answers web UI questions.

g.text: contacts · contacts listed in channels.<type>.dm_allowlist send a message to your DartClaw number or bot
The sample lists WhatsApp contacts; Signal, Google Chat and Slack work the same way and all write to the same memory.
DM access gate · with dm_access: allowlist only senders in dm_allowlist are processed; an unlisted sender gets no response
Add or remove a contact without a restart through the allowlist API or the web UI at /settings/channels/<type>.
contact session · dm_scope: per-contact gives each contact one session, shared across channels; the default keeps one per channel
Messages in quick succession join into one turn (channels.debounce_window_ms, default 1000); sessions.maintenance archives idle sessions.
guard chain · the guard chain bounds what the agent may do with the message: command, file, network and tool policy
guards.content also classifies agent-boundary and fetched content for safety.
behavior files · SOUL.md carries the extraction rules and storage format, USER.md the contact directory
The agent reads them each turn, so editing a rule changes the next message without a restart.
extract · the agent pulls action items, deadlines, commitments and contact details out of a casual message
It works from the sender in the message metadata and the rules in SOUL.md; the raw inbound text is processed as sent.
memory_apply · reads the current collection and entry revisions, then submits one atomic change set per request
A stale revision is refused, so the agent re-reads and retries instead of overwriting; data is topic entries, not a database.
reply · a brief confirmation goes back to the sender on the same channel
Outbound redaction strips secrets from the reply; the raw inbound message was still seen by the agent.
web UI · you ask later in the web UI, for example about action items or last week's conversations
A web chat turn skips the DM access gate: it is you, not a contact.
memory_search · the agent searches memory and returns structured results to the web chat
Not a real CRM: complex queries such as all contacts in London with overdue tasks may come back approximate.
memory · canonical memory topic entries: contacts, action-items and notes, plus daily-crm-summary when the job runs
All channels write here, so contact history is unified; sessions are pruned, memory is not.
crm-daily-summary · optional cron prompt: reviews the day's interactions and saves a summary under topic daily-crm-summary
delivery: announce sends it to active DM sessions and web clients; the recipe works without it.
